title: [WA] Greyhound Adoption $75 (Usually $200) @ Greyhounds as Pets
body:
Deal: [WA] Greyhound Adoption $75 (Usually $200) @ Greyhounds as Pets

[sgrusty] For potential new dog owners also be aware, the big cost to factor in is usually the vet bills.. they also require dentist work, health checks etc which ain't cheap. This is on top of regular deworm / flea meds etc..
They are awesome to have if you can afford and can commit to a dog financially and also cater to their needs like daily walks etc…
[nosytt] Uh really?
I've had two greyhounds now and never took them to the vet, they lived very happy lives.
[AngoraFish] Sadly, mine have cost me many thousands of dollars. Teeth and dental issues, foot corns, skin tearing, arthritis. Vet bills can add up very quickly.
[Sprezza] Don't know what you got down voted!
I agree. Easy care animals. Much easier than other pure breds with less genetic issues. Biggest problem would be them injuring themselves as they're absolutely d-heads.
[PurpleMonkeyDwasher] Every dog is expensive really. They're a luxury. They don't necessarily need a lot of dental work. Every dog is different and depends what you feed them too. Having the free time to take them for walks is also a luxury that not everyone has. Everyone has different circumstances however if they can, they'll pick up a new best friend pretty cheap. I've got to say, if you're worried your dog might have issues taking up pet insurance isn't a bad idea. It's very expensive once they have existing conditions but in the early stages it can be helpful.
[FrugalDealSeeker] I have a border collie with floppy ears unfortunately he keeps getting ear infections costing us ~$500 for each vet visit inc. medication. Insurance is a huge saver here.
[PurpleMonkeyDwasher] We used to call insurance "the charity" or "the rich uncle" at the start. Our dog had a lot more issues than expected. Unfortunately then they jacked up the premium over time however we negotiate every year as it does get ridiculous.
[banana365] This whole program is part of the window dressing by those that promote and participate in the barbaric practice of greyhound racing. "Look, we don't kill all the failures now, we let people have some of them as pets." Sure, this gives a few a better life, but far, far better just to ban greyhound racing, as has been done elsewhere.
https://kb.rspca.org.au/categories/sport-entertainment-and-w…
[JoeyJoeJoe] And because they didn’t even race these dogs this deal gets a downvote?
[AngoraFish] One of my adopted greyhounds ran in 50 races. The other was bred and trained for racing but in the end was too small and slow to be competitive. Both would still have been bred and both would have been put down if we hadn't adopted them.
[OZKap] Zero chance they're breeding these to sell for $75, even $200.
Designer dogs go for $1000+
[PurpleMonkeyDwasher] Well-bred racing greyhounds can sell for $5,000 to $25,000 each. The $75 is almost certainly an adoption fee, not what it costs to breed one!
And greyhounds are hardly a new designer breed. Greyhound-like dogs were depicted in ancient Egypt thousands of years ago. They've been fashionable for a few millennia. 😂
[Bytelover] Better off going through GAWA, real volunteers and not supported by the industry https://greyhoundadoptionswa.com.au/
[DingoBlue] Banning that crap displayed massive balls in NSW then they reversed it.
[PurpleMonkeyDwasher] It's just making the best of a crap situation. It's not their fault they're beautiful loving sentient beings bred into that industry but they deserve to live beyond their racing days.
[banana365] It helps perpetuate it. It lessens the ire directed at them because they're doing "something good" by re-homing dogs that would be otherwise killed due to being of no use any more. It allows the trade to go on longer, perhaps for many more years, churning out more dogs that will inevitably suffer during their hard life and have a premature death inflicted on them.
But sure they're "making the best" of it 🙄
[Jimothy Wongingtons] Can’t I just bet that all the dogs will have a good time?
[McMaferMur] the mini version of this breed is sooooooooooooooo cute.
[ticket65] Not the dogs fault. I have an adopted dog, and it's such a wonderful pet. Biggest lapdog you'll ever find….
[banana365] Absolutely nobody is claiming it's the dogs' fault. It is 100% on the shoulders of the dog racing community.
[Seancohen] We just adopted a greyhound 3 weeks ago, in NSW through a private rehoming agency.
Best decision we made, she's beautiful.
But relating to the industry is complicated. They are full of bastards that will kill anything that's not making money. The dogs are livestock to them, the way we think of chicken or lamb.
Our girl ran 8 races then had an injury. If she hadn't found a home she'd be done for.
So, should racing dogs be legal? I don't think so.
But do these dogs exist, and will they be killed if they're not rehomed? Yes.
However you feel about the industry and what should happen, these dogs exist right now.
[PurpleMonkeyDwasher] Congrats on the adoption. Lovely cause. Greyhounds are the best.
[banana365] And the public relations drive of dog adoption helps perpetuate the barbarism of dog racing. As horrible as it is, not adopting the current batch of "no longer useful" dogs makes it more likely that there would be no future breeding of dogs that are born into a terrible life.
This is the only reason they do this.
A few decades ago my wife used to walk home past Cannington dog track. She started walking a longer way home because she could not handle seeing bins with dead dogs sticking out of them.
All that's changed is they're better at hiding the reality from the public.
